name: Nursing Speak-Up & Safety Challenge
description: Evaluates a nurse raising a safety concern with a more senior clinician — questioning an order, flagging a missed check, or refusing to proceed until a discrepancy is resolved — assertively and respectfully in English.

anchors.80-100: Clear, fluent phrasing under interpersonal pressure; the concern survives the stress intact.
anchors.50-70: Understandable but hesitations or grammar errors weaken the message when pushed back on.
anchors.10-40: Frequent errors that obscure what the safety concern actually is.

anchors.80-100: States the specific discrepancy and the specific patient risk in one clear sentence, early.
anchors.50-70: Raises a concern but leaves the listener to work out what exactly is wrong.
anchors.10-40: Hints at discomfort without ever naming the discrepancy or the risk.

anchors.80-100: Escalates in steps — asks, states the concern, states the risk, then states that they cannot proceed — and holds the position under pushback.
anchors.50-70: Raises the concern once, then defers as soon as the senior clinician pushes back.
anchors.10-40: Backs down immediately, or jumps straight to confrontation without asking first.

anchors.80-100: Frames the concern around the patient rather than the colleague; stays collegial while holding the line.
anchors.50-70: Respectful but over-apologizes to the point of undercutting the concern.
anchors.10-40: Accusatory, or so indirect that the concern reads as personal reluctance.

anchors.80-100: Confirms the corrected order or plan explicitly, reads it back, and states what they will do next.
anchors.50-70: Reaches a resolution but never confirms it in words.
anchors.10-40: Leaves the discrepancy unresolved or ambiguous.

checklist.item: Raised the concern before carrying out the questioned action
Named the specific discrepancy (what was ordered vs. what is expected)
Named the specific patient risk, not just personal discomfort
Used graded assertiveness — asked first, then escalated the wording if dismissed
Held the position under pushback rather than deferring to seniority
Framed the concern around patient safety, not the colleague's competence
Confirmed and read back the corrected order or agreed plan
